_note: Single source of truth for the MoP fitting parameters used by every experiment. Before this file existed the same values were copied into five scripts and the config files only documented them, so a change to one copy would silently disagree with the others. Scripts load this file through common/params.py and none of them may hard-code these values.
_lambda_u_note: ridge on the utilities; small enough not to shrink them
_lambda_pi_note: Dirichlet concentration on the mixture weights; 1 is the uniform prior
_lambda_sigma_note: lambda_sigma = 0.02 * nJ, i.e. nJ / 50, with nJ the number of judgments in the fitted subset. This was written as 0.05 when the file was first created, which is a different prior by a factor of 2.5: 1/50 = 0.02, and 0.05 would be nJ/20. The mistake was caught because the case study stopped reproducing its recorded output: at 0.05 the corpus pBIC curve put its minimum at K=3 instead of at K=4. It is the strength of a single-parameter prior, so lambda_sigma > 2 is what the prior mean needs, not the mode; with nJ = 5401 it is 108.02.
_prior_mode_phi0_note: Scale parameter of the inverse-gamma prior on the dispersion, not a quantity the model estimates. 'data' uses mop.inference.prior_mode_phi0(X, y), the pooled residual scale of the fitted subset, which is what the case study uses. The simulation passes its design dispersion (0.05) explicitly, because there the pooled residual measures the between-component variance rather than the within-component scale the prior is meant to describe.
_max_components_note: computational search limit, applied together with the ordinal bound: the grid stops at min(A!, max_components), so a problem with A = 2 alternatives is searched to 2 components and one with A = 4 to 9. A! is the number of strict preference orderings; beyond it at least two components share an ordering by the pigeonhole principle.
